l: creation of the good spirit, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XII.
s: The creation of the good spirit is directly and indirectly defiled by the living Ashemaogha. A dead stranger does not directly or indirectly defile it in the same manner.

l: good spirit, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XII.
s: The good spirit's creatures are directly and indirectly defiled by the living Ashemaogha. His actions include striking water, extinguishing fire, carrying off the cow, killing the faithful man, and depriving him of necessities.

l: Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIII.
s: This unit concerns Ahura Mazda’s teachings about dogs, their protection of people and property, and penalties for harming or neglecting them. It identifies the dog Vanghâpara as a good creature of the good spirit and the daêva Zairimyangura as an evil creature of the evil spirit. It classifies shepherd’s dogs, house dogs, Vohunazga dogs, young dogs, mad dogs, and water dogs, describing their duties, treatment, and punishments connected with them. It also teaches that killing a water dog causes drought until the murderer is killed and a sacrifice is offered.

l: Ahura Mazda, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIII.
s: Ahura Mazda identifies the good and evil creatures associated with nighttime destruction, prescribes penalties for harming or neglecting dogs, and explains the duties and qualities of different dogs. He says that he made the dog watchful, wakeful, sharp-toothed, and strong against evil-doers, and that a sacrifice restores the land after a water dog is killed.

l: good spirit, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIII.
s: The good spirit has creatures including the dog Vanghâpara, which kills thousands of the evil spirit’s creatures from midnight until sunrise. The dog is described as one of the good spirit’s most valuable creatures.

l: evil spirit, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIII.
s: The evil spirit has creatures including the daêva Zairimyangura, which kills thousands of the good spirit’s creatures from midnight until sunrise.

l: dog, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIII.
s: The dog is regarded as a protective creature that watches over people’s goods and helps guard houses and folds. It has qualities compared with eight kinds of people and should be fed milk, fat, and meat. Different kinds of dogs receive defined protections, duties, and penalties for injury or death.

l: dog Vanghâpara, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIII.
s: The dog Vanghâpara, also called Duzaka by evil-speaking people, has a prickly back and a long, thin muzzle. It kills thousands of the evil spirit’s creatures from midnight until sunrise, and killing it brings severe penalties unless the killer atones by offering a sacrifice to Sraosha.

l: shepherd's dog, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIII.
s: The shepherd’s dog goes around the fold watching for thieves and wolves and is protected from being struck or killed. Bad food given to it incurs the guilt associated with mistreating a high-ranking master, and its death carries eight hundred stripes with each of two instruments. It and the house dog must not be kept away when passing a faithful person’s house.

l: house dog, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIII.
s: The house dog goes around the house watching for thieves and wolves and protects household goods. Bad food given to it incurs the guilt associated with mistreating a master of middle rank, and its death carries seven hundred stripes with each of two instruments.

l: Vohunazga dog, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIII.
s: The Vohunazga dog claims none of the shepherd’s or house dog’s talents and seeks only its subsistence. Bad food given to it incurs the guilt associated with mistreating a holy priest, and its death carries six hundred stripes with each of two instruments.

l: water dog, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIII.
s: The water dog is formed at the spring of the waters from the ghosts of dead dogs and she-dogs. Killing a water dog causes a drought that deprives the land of sweetness, fatness, health, healing, and growth until the murderer is killed and a sacrifice is offered for the dog.

l: mad dog, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIII.
s: A mad dog, or one that bites without barking, must be restrained with a wooden collar and tied to a post. If it harms a sheep or a person, its right ear, left ear, right foot, left foot, and finally tail are cut off for successive offenses; if it is not restrained, those responsible incur penalties.

l: wolf, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIII.
s: The wolf is treated as a danger against which shepherd’s and house dogs must watch. A wolf born of a he-dog and a she-wolf is said to be more murderous and destructive than one born of a she-dog and a he-wolf, and it deserves more to be killed.

l: sacrifice, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIII.
s: A sacrifice to Sraosha can atone for killing the dog Vanghâpara. After a water dog is killed, a sacrifice for three days and three nights with fire, tied baresma, and uplifted Haoma is required before the land’s sweetness, fatness, health, and growth return.

l: Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIV.
s: Fargard XIV. records Zarathustra’s question to Ahura Mazda about the penalty for killing a water dog. Ahura Mazda prescribes extensive atonements, including stripes, offerings, killing harmful creatures, repairing or providing implements and buildings, giving land and livestock, and performing other acts for godly men. The atonement includes a rill of running water, a piece of arable land, a house with ox-stalls, and a virgin maid. Whoever completes the penalty enters the world of the holy ones, while whoever does not falls into the world of the wicked.

l: Fargard XIV., Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIV.
s: Fargard XIV. sets out the penalty and atonement for killing a water dog, as given by Ahura Mazda in answer to Zarathustra.

l: Zarathustra, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIV.
s: Zarathustra asks Ahura Mazda what penalty must be paid by one who kills a water dog.

l: Ahura Mazda, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIV.
s: Ahura Mazda prescribes the penalties and atonements for killing a water dog, including stripes, offerings, gifts, repairs, killings of harmful creatures, and provisions for godly men. He also explains the required sizes or values of the silver, gold, rill, land, house, and virgin maid.

l: water dog, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIV.
s: A water dog is described as one born from a thousand dogs and a thousand she-dogs. Killing one so that it dies and its soul parts from its body incurs the stated penalty.

l: soul of the water dog, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIV.
s: The prescribed works, offerings, gifts, and acts of repair are performed as atonement unto the soul of the water dog.

l: penalty for killing a water dog, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIV.
s: The penalty includes ten thousand stripes with the Aspahê-astra and ten thousand with the Sraoshô-karana, along with many prescribed atonements. These include offerings to the fire of Ahura Mazda, killing harmful creatures, filling holes, giving implements, providing land and buildings, and other acts.

l: Fire, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIV.
s: The offender must bring ten thousand loads of hard, well-dried wood and ten thousand loads of soft or sweet-scented wood to the fire of Ahura Mazda as atonement.

l: godly men, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIV.
s: Godly men receive implements, war equipment, husbandmen’s tools, land, a house, beds, small cattle, and other provisions as part of the atonement. They are also treated to their fill of meat, bread, strong drink, and wine.

l: rill of running water, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIV.
s: A rill of running water must be procured for godly husbandmen. Its depth and breadth must each be that of a dog, and it must water the piece of arable land on both sides.

l: piece of arable land, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIV.
s: A piece of arable land must be given to godly men. It must be as much land as can be watered with the prescribed rill on both sides.

l: house with ox-stalls, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIV.
s: A house with ox-stalls must be procured for godly men, measuring nine hâthras and nine nematas. Its largest part must be twelve Vîtâras, its middle part nine Vîtâras, and its smallest part six Vîtâras.

l: virgin maid, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIV.
s: A virgin maid whom no man has known must be given to a godly man. She is specified as a sister or daughter of the offender, at puberty, with ear-rings, and past her fifteenth year.

l: world of the holy ones, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIV.
s: Anyone who undergoes the prescribed atonement enters the world of the holy ones.

l: world of the wicked, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIV.
s: Anyone who does not undergo the prescribed atonement falls into the world of the wicked, described as a dark world made of darkness and the offspring of darkness.

l: godly and piously giving and procuring, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIV.
s: Godly and pious giving and procuring form a major part of the required atonement. The offender must provide offerings, tools, animals, land, water, buildings, beds, and other goods for godly men and husbandmen.

l: Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XV.
s: Fargard XV concerns five unconfessed and unatoned sins that make a committer a Peshôtanu, including teaching a wrong creed, harming dogs, harming a pregnant bitch, intercourse with a menstruating woman, and intercourse with a pregnant woman when mischief follows. It also concerns damsels who conceive, induced miscarriage, and the duties of men and others to support pregnant females and their offspring. Ahura Mazda teaches that the faithful must support pregnant women and bitches, with failure causing the penalty for wilful murder. The unit further describes breeding a bitch with three dogs and the penalty for striking her after she has milk and bears a young one.

l: Fargard XV, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XV.
s: Fargard XV sets out five sins that make a committer a Peshôtanu and gives teachings about pregnancy, miscarriage, support for pregnant females, and breeding a bitch with three dogs.

l: Ahura Mazda, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XV.
s: Ahura Mazda answers Zarathustra's questions about sins, miscarriage, support for pregnant females, the care of young dogs, and breeding a bitch with three dogs. He states the penalties and duties described in the unit.

l: Peshôtanu, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XV.
s: Peshôtanu is the condition made by committing one of five specified sins without confession or atonement.

l: worshippers of Mazda, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XV.
s: The faithful are to look after every pregnant female, whether two-footed or four-footed, woman or bitch. They are also told how to support a pregnant bitch according to where she is found.

l: man, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XV.
s: A man makes himself a Peshôtanu by teaching a faithful person a foreign wrong creed or law, giving harmful bones or hot food to a dog, smiting or frightening a pregnant bitch so that she dies, or having intercourse with a pregnant woman when mischief follows and she dies. A man who causes a damsel's miscarriage shares the sin with the damsel and the old woman, and a man who conceives a child with a damsel must support her until the child is born.

l: damsel, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XV.
s: A damsel who conceives is told not to produce menses against the course of nature or destroy the fruit in her womb from dread of the people. If she causes the fruit to perish, the sin and the murder are on both her and the father, and she pays the penalty for wilful murder.

l: woman, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XV.
s: Intercourse with a woman who has an issue of blood is one of the five sins that makes a man a Peshôtanu. Intercourse with a woman quick with child makes a man a Peshôtanu if mischief follows and she dies.

l: bitch, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XV.
s: A bitch that is big with young must be supported until the whelps are born, with responsibility assigned according to where she is lying. A bitch covered by three dogs is watched until she brings forth a young one, and striking her after she has milk brings seven hundred stripes with each of two instruments.

l: young dogs, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XV.
s: Young dogs are considered capable of self-defence and self-subsistence when they can run about in a circuit of twice seven houses. They are to be supported for six months.

l: child, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XV.
s: A child is to be supported for seven years.

l: sins that make a committer a Peshôtanu, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XV.
s: There are five such sins: teaching a faithful person a foreign wrong creed or law knowingly, giving bones or hot food that harms a dog and causes its death, smiting or frightening a pregnant bitch so that she dies, intercourse with a woman who has an issue of blood, and intercourse with a pregnant woman when mischief follows and she dies.

l: harming a pregnant bitch, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XV.
s: Smiting a pregnant bitch or frightening her by chasing, shouting, or clapping is a sin that makes the man a Peshôtanu if she falls into a hole, well, precipice, river, or canal and dies.

l: pregnancy, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XV.
s: A man who causes a damsel to conceive must support her until the child is born. Pregnant bitches must likewise be supported until the whelps are born, and Âtar watches over a pregnant bitch as well as over a woman.

l: induced miscarriage, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XV.
s: A damsel is told not to produce menses or destroy the fruit in her womb from dread of the people. If a man orders it and an old woman uses Banga, Shaêta, Ghnâna, Fraspâta, or another drug to cause miscarriage, the sin is on the man, the damsel, and the old woman.

l: supporting a pregnant female, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XV.
s: The faithful must support every pregnant female. For a pregnant bitch, the person responsible is determined by the place where she lies, and in a pasture-field she is taken to rest on a litter of suitable foliage until the young dogs can defend and support themselves.

l: wilful murder penalty, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XV.
s: Failure to support a pregnant damsel or pregnant bitch, when the child or whelps come to mischief for want of proper support, requires payment of the penalty for wilful murder. The damsel and her father also pay that penalty when she destroys the fruit in her womb.

l: breeding a bitch with three dogs, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XV.
s: To have a bitch covered so that the offspring is strong, worshippers of Mazda dig a hole in the earth, keep the bitch far from children and Fire, and let three dogs approach her one after another while watching her.

l: three dogs, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XV.
s: Three dogs cover the bitch one after another, each kept apart from the former so that they do not assail one another. The bitch then grows big with young, her milk comes to her teats, and she brings forth a young one born from three dogs.

l: Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVI.
s: This unit concerns the treatment and seclusion of a woman who has an issue of blood in the house of a worshipper of Mazda. Ahura Mazda commands that she be kept away from the fire, water, consecrated bundles of baresma, and faithful, and that food be brought to her from three paces away in vessels of common metal. The woman remains in the place of infirmity while the issue continues, and she is washed with gômêz and water. It also sets penalties for suppressing the issue, repeatedly touching her, and having sexual intercourse with her.

l: Ahura Mazda, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVI.
s: Ahura Mazda answers questions about the treatment of a woman who has an issue of blood. He commands her seclusion, specifies distances from the fire, water, consecrated bundles of baresma, and faithful, and prescribes penalties for violations.

l: worshippers of Mazda, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVI.
s: The worshippers of Mazda must clear the way of wood, strew dry dust, erect a building for the woman, provide her food from three paces away, and wash her with gômêz and water. They must also kill specified Khrafstras and must not suppress her issue.

l: woman who has an issue of blood, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVI.
s: The woman is kept in a separate building and must remain three paces from the faithful, fifteen paces from the fire and water, and fifteen paces from the consecrated bundles of baresma. She remains in the place of infirmity as long as she continues to see blood and is washed with gômêz and water.

l: place of infirmity, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVI.
s: The place of infirmity is where the woman sits while she continues to see blood after successive nights. She remains there until the prescribed number of nights has passed.

l: Fire, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVI.
s: The fire must be kept fifteen paces from the woman. Her building must be erected higher than the house so that her look does not fall upon the fire.

l: water, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVI.
s: The water must be kept fifteen paces from the woman. Water is also used to wash her by one of three holes dug in the earth.

l: blood, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVI.
s: The woman may continue to see blood after three through nine nights. If she still sees blood after nine nights, the condition is called a work of the Daêvas.

l: issue of blood, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVI.
s: The issue of blood may occur out of the ordinary course or at the usual period. Suppressing it incurs two hundred stripes with the Aspahê-astra and two hundred with the Sraoshô-karana.

l: intercourse with a menstruating woman, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVI.
s: Sexual intercourse with a woman who has an issue of blood is condemned as an extremely grave act. A person who lies with her in sexual intercourse is described as an ungodly man who must pay for it with his life.

l: Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVII.
s: Zarathustra asks Ahura Mazda which deed most increases the baleful strength of the Daêvas. Ahura Mazda says that dropping combed hair, shaved hair, or pared nails into a hole or crack without observing the lawful rites produces Daêvas and lice in the earth. He prescribes distances, holes, furrows, spoken words, and repeated recitation of the Ahuna-Vairya for disposing of hair and nails, warning that undedicated nails become weapons for the Mâzainya Daêvas.

l: Zarathustra, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVII.
s: Zarathustra asks Ahura Mazda which deed most increases the baleful strength of the Daêvas. He receives instructions for disposing of hair and nails according to the lawful rites.

l: Ahura Mazda, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVII.
s: Ahura Mazda identifies improperly discarded hair and nails as a deed that increases the baleful strength of the Daêvas. He gives Zarathustra rules for distances, holes, spoken words, furrows, and recitations.

l: Daêvas, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVII.
s: Daêvas are produced in the earth when hair or nails are dropped into a hole or crack without the lawful rites. The deed is said to increase their baleful strength.

l: hair, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVII.
s: Hair that is combed or shaved off must be taken away from the faithful, fire, water, and consecrated bundles of baresma. It is placed in a deep hole with fiend-smiting words, furrows, and recitations of the Ahuna-Vairya.

l: nails, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVII.
s: Nails that are pared off must be buried in a hole outside the house, as deep as the top joint of the little finger. They must be accompanied by spoken words, furrows, recitations of the Ahuna-Vairya, and dedication to the Ashô-zusta bird.

l: lawful rites, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVII.
s: The lawful rites must be observed when hair or nails are disposed of. Without them, Daêvas and lice are produced in the earth.

l: hole, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVII.
s: A hole is used for disposing of hair and nails. Its required depth differs according to the hardness of the earth for hair and is as deep as the top joint of the little finger for nails.

l: Ahuna-Vairya, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVII.
s: The Ahuna-Vairya is chanted three, six, or nine times after furrows are drawn around the hole.

l: Mâzainya fiends, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVII.
s: Mâzainya Daêvas may receive undedicated nails as weapons, including spears, knives, bows, falcon-winged arrows, and sling-stones. Dedicated nails are invoked as weapons against them.

l: Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: Ahura Mazda teaches Zarathustra who may be called an Âthravan, what increases the unseen power of Death, and how Sraosha, Fire, and Parôdars oppose harmful forces. The unit describes the Drug’s four males and the acts that cause or counteract her offspring, including neglect of wealth-sharing, improper urination, nocturnal emission, and going without the sacred girdle and sacred shirt after fifteen. Ahura Mazda also describes Gahi’s harm and prescribes severe atonement for intercourse with a woman who has an issue of blood. Those who fulfill the required atonement enter the world of the holy ones, while those who do not fall into the world of the wicked.

l: Ahura Mazda, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: Ahura Mazda teaches Zarathustra about Âthravan conduct, the causes of the unseen power of Death, Sraosha, Fire, Parôdars, the Drug, Gahi, and the required atonement. He says that those who pay the prescribed atonement enter the world of the holy ones, while those who do not fall into the world of the wicked.

l: Zarathustra, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: Zarathustra asks Ahura Mazda what increases the unseen power of Death, who is the Sraosha-varez of Sraosha, who grieves Ahura Mazda most, and what atonement is required for intercourse with a woman who has an issue of blood.

l: Âthravan, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: An Âthravan is not one who merely wears a Paitidâna, holds a Khrafstraghna or twig, or wields the Astra mairya without being girded with the law. An Âthravan performs worship, learns and teaches, and sits up at night seeking holy Wisdom.

l: paradise, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: Paradise is reached by the Âthravan at the head of the Kinvat bridge and by the person who first rises and brings clean wood to Fire. Giving a pair of Parôdars birds or feeding a Parôdars bird also leads directly to paradise.

l: teaching a foreign wrong creed, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: The man who teaches a wrong law is identified as increasing the unseen power of Death.

l: sacred girdle, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: The sacred girdle is worn by the Âthravan and is required, along with the sacred shirt, for a person over fifteen to avoid being withered by the Daêvas. A person who continues for three years without wearing it, chanting the Gâthas, or worshipping the good waters increases the unseen power of Death.

l: Sraosha, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: Sraosha is described as holy, strong, tall-formed, and the incarnate Word. He brings clean wood to Fire, wakes Parôdars, and questions the Drug about her four males and the means of counteracting them.

l: Parôdars, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: Parôdars is the bird that ill-speaking people call Kahrkatâs. It lifts its voice against the dawn, calls people to rise and recite the Ashem yad vahistem, and is associated with blessings, paradise, and the giving of a male and female pair.

l: Bûshyãsta, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: Bûshyãsta is the long-handed one who comes upon the living world after it wakes and urges people to sleep because the time has not yet come.

l: Daêvas, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: The Daêvas make Âzi and oppose Fire. They wither a person over fifteen who walks without the sacred girdle or sacred shirt, leaving that person able to destroy the world of the holy spirit like the Yâtus and Zandas.

l: good thoughts, good words, and good deeds, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: Good thoughts, good words, and good deeds are three excellent things for which people must never be slack. Fire blesses the person who brings him clean wood with growth of herds and sons, and with mastery of the vow by the mind and soul.

l: bad thoughts, bad words, and bad deeds, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: Bad thoughts, bad words, and bad deeds are three abominable things for which people must always be slack.

l: Fire, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: Fire, the son of Ahura Mazda, calls the master of the house and the husbandman for clean wood during the first and second parts of the night. In the third part he calls Sraosha, and he blesses the person who brings him dry, clean wood with well-washed hands.

l: Âzi, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: Âzi, made by the Daêvas, strives against Fire and wants to put out Fire’s life.

l: Drug, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: The Drug is a wretched and wicked demon who says that four males make her conceive progeny. These are the person who refuses a small gift, the man who lets urine fall along the upper forepart of his foot, the man who emits seed during sleep, and a person over fifteen who goes without the sacred girdle or sacred shirt.

l: Ârmaiti Spenta, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: Spenta Ârmaiti is described as being clad in grass, and Gahi’s look withers one third of that grass. The man who emits seed during sleep is delivered to Spenta Ârmaiti and is to be returned against the day of resurrection as one who knows the Gâthas, Yasna, and revealed law.

l: Gahi, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: Gahi is said to go a-whoring after the faithful and unfaithful, the worshippers of Mazda and the worshippers of the Daêvas, the wicked and the righteous. Her look and touch wither parts of floods, plants, grass, and the faithful person’s good thoughts, good words, good deeds, strength, fiend-killing power, and holiness.

l: issue of blood, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: An issue of blood may occur out of the ordinary course or at the usual period. Intercourse with a woman who has an issue of blood, when both parties act knowingly and willingly, requires the stated atonement.

l: atonement, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: The atonement includes killing or offering specified animals, offering wood, consecrating baresma, making Zaothra-libations with Haoma and meat, killing snakes, frogs, and ants, throwing thirty bridges over canals, and undergoing a thousand stripes with each of the Aspahê-astra and Sraoshô-karana.

l: world of the holy ones, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: The world of the holy ones is entered by the person who pays the prescribed atonement.

l: world of the wicked, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XVIII.
s: The world of the wicked is a dark world made of darkness and the offspring of darkness. The person who does not pay the prescribed atonement falls into it.

l: Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIX.
s: Angra Mainyu sends the Drug to destroy Zarathustra, but Zarathustra repels it by chanting the Ahuna-Vairya and refuses to renounce the good law of the worshippers of Mazda. Zarathustra asks Ahura Mazda how to cleanse Vohu-manô and people from defilement, and Ahura Mazda instructs him to invoke sacred beings and perform prescribed rites. Ahura Mazda also describes the soul’s journey after death: the soul of the righteous crosses the Kinvad bridge, is guided by the well-shapen maid, and reaches Garô-nmânem. The Daêvas flee from Zarathustra and retreat into the depths of hell.

l: Angra Mainyu, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIX.
s: Angra Mainyu sends the Drug to destroy Zarathustra and later urges him to renounce the good law of the worshippers of Mazda. Zarathustra refuses and declares that the sacred Word, the sacred mortar, the sacred cup, and the Haoma are weapons against Angra Mainyu and his creation.

l: Zarathustra, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIX.
s: Zarathustra repels the Drug by chanting the Ahuna-Vairya and refuses to renounce the good law of the worshippers of Mazda. He asks Ahura Mazda how to cleanse Vohu-manô and people from defilement, performs the instructed invocations and rites, and invokes the holy creation of Ahura Mazda.

l: Ahura Mazda, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIX.
s: Ahura Mazda teaches Zarathustra how to drive away the Drug, cleanse Vohu-manô, and cleanse faithful people. He instructs Zarathustra in invocations, sacrifices, purification rites, and the fate of souls after death.

l: Daêvas, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIX.
s: The Daêvas seek Zarathustra’s death, but they are repelled by him and flee with shouts and evil looks to the head of Arezûra. They run away into the depths of the dark, horrid world of hell.

l: Drug, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIX.
s: The Drug, identified as the demon Bûiti and the unseen death, rushes to destroy Zarathustra but is dismayed by the Ahuna-Vairya and flees. It later appears as an enemy opposed by Zarathustra and the good creatures.

l: incarnate Word, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIX.
s: The sacred Word is one of Zarathustra’s best weapons against Angra Mainyu and his creation. Spenta Mainyu gave it to Zarathustra in the boundless Time, and the Amesha Spentas gave it to him as well.

l: Ahuna-Vairya, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIX.
s: The Ahuna-Vairya is chanted by Zarathustra to repel the Drug and is identified as a weapon against Angra Mainyu. It is also recited two hundred times in the cleansing rite for Vohu-manô.

l: law of Mazda, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIX.
s: The good law of the worshippers of Mazda is a law Zarathustra refuses to renounce even if his body, life, and soul should burst. Ahura Mazda identifies it as a law that destroys fiends.

l: the Amesha Spentas, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIX.
s: The Amesha Spentas give Zarathustra the sacred Word and are invoked as rulers over the seven Karshvares of the earth. They are honored with sacrifice and are associated with their golden seat and Garô-nmânem.

l: Vohu-manô, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIX.
s: Vohu-manô is directly and indirectly defiled by the Daêvas and must be cleansed. Ahura Mazda prescribes washing Vohu-manô with gômêz and water, laying it under the heavens for nine nights, and perfuming it by the fire.

l: Sraosha, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIX.
s: Sraosha is invoked as holy, tall-formed, and carrying a club to strike the heads of fiends. He is worshipped with sacrifice and is said to smite the fiend Kunda.

l: death, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIX.
s: The Drug is called the unseen death and is described as hell-born. After a man dies and his time is over, the hellish Daêvas assail him and the soul enters the way made by Time.

l: the soul of the righteous, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIX.
s: The soul of the righteous is guided by the well-shapen maid across the Kinvad bridge and is placed in the presence of the heavenly gods. It then passes to the golden seat of Ahura Mazda, the Amesha Spentas, and Garô-nmânem.

l: the Kinvad bridge, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIX.
s: The Kinvad bridge is the holy bridge made by Mazda at the head of which souls are asked for the reward of the worldly goods they gave away. The well-shapen maid places the soul of the righteous above the bridge in the presence of the heavenly gods.

l: the well-shapen maid, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIX.
s: The well-shapen maid comes with dogs at her sides and can distinguish, is graceful, does what she wants, and has high understanding. She makes the soul of the righteous go above Hara-berezati and places it above the Kinvad bridge before the heavenly gods.

l: Garô-nmânem, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XIX.
s: Garô-nmânem is the abode of Ahura Mazda, the Amesha Spentas, and all other holy beings. The souls of the righteous pass to it after reaching the golden seat.

l: Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XX.
s: The unit concerns Thrita, whom Ahura Mazda identifies as the first healer among the strong men of yore. Thrita drove back sickness and death and turned away the point of the poniard and the fire of fever from mortal bodies. He obtained a source of remedies, while Ahura Mazda brought down healing plants growing around Gaokerena. The text invokes health upon mortal bodies and commands sickness, death, pain, fever, disease, the Drug, and other harmful beings to depart.

l: Thrita, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XX.
s: Thrita was the first of the healthful, wise, happy, wealthy, glorious, and strong men of yore to drive back sickness and death and turn away the point of the poniard and the fire of fever from mortal bodies. He asked for and obtained a source of remedies.

l: Zarathustra, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XX.
s: Zarathustra asked Ahura Mazda who first drove back sickness and death and turned away the point of the poniard and the fire of fever from mortal bodies.

l: Ahura Mazda, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XX.
s: Ahura Mazda identified Thrita as the first healer and said that Thrita obtained a source of remedies. Ahura Mazda also brought down the healing plants that grow around Gaokerena and invoked health upon mortal bodies.

l: Angra Mainyu, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XX.
s: Angra Mainyu created sickness, rottenness, and infection by witchcraft against the bodies of mortals.

l: Airyaman, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XX.
s: Airyaman is called upon to come for the men and women of Zarathustra and the faithful to rejoice. He is also called upon to smite diseases, deaths, the Yâtus, Pairikas, and wicked Gainis.

l: Drug, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XX.
s: The Drug is to be smitten by the might of the invoked powers. It is commanded to perish and depart to the regions of the north.

l: health and healing, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XX.
s: Health is invoked upon the bodies of mortals by blessing-spells, prayers, and praises.

l: sickness, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XX.
s: Sickness was driven back by Thrita and is commanded to depart. Ahura Mazda says he drives it away.

l: death, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XX.
s: Death was driven back by Thrita and is commanded to depart. Ahura Mazda says he drives it away, and Airyaman is called upon to smite deaths.

l: pain, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XX.
s: Pain is commanded to depart, and Ahura Mazda says he drives it away.

l: fever, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XX.
s: The fire of fever was turned away from mortal bodies by Thrita. Fever is commanded to depart, and Ahura Mazda says he drives it away.

l: diseases (created by Angra Mainyu), Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XX.
s: Disease was created by Angra Mainyu through witchcraft against mortal bodies. It is commanded to depart, and Ahura Mazda says he drives it away.

l: healing plants, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XX.
s: Ahura Mazda brought down healing plants that grow by many hundreds, thousands, and myriads around Gaokerena.

l: source of remedies, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XX.
s: Thrita asked for a source of remedies and obtained it from Khshathra-Vairya to withstand sickness, death, pain, fever, disease, rottenness, and infection.

l: bodies of mortals, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XX.
s: The bodies of mortals are afflicted by sickness, rottenness, and infection created by Angra Mainyu. Health is invoked upon them, and Thrita first turned away the point of the poniard and the fire of fever from them.

l: Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXI.
s: Fargard XXI concerns waters, light, healing, fertility, and the driving away of sickness, death, and hostile beings. It calls on clouds, the sun, moon, and stars to rise and bring waters, light, growth, health, and healing. It describes holy spells that purify children and women and make women rich in children and milk. It invokes Airyaman and other sacred formulas against diseases, deaths, Yâtus, Pairikas, Gainis, and the fiendish Drug.

l: Fargard XXI, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXI.
s: Fargard XXI concerns waters and light, including their power to bring growth, health, healing, and protection from sickness and death.

l: holy bull, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXI.
s: The holy bull is hailed as beneficent and as one who makes increase and growth. He bestows gifts upon the excellent faithful and the faithful yet unborn, but is killed by the Gahi, the ungodly Ashemaogha, and the wicked tyrant.

l: Zarathustra, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXI.
s: Holy Zarathustra is addressed in the instruction that calls the clouds to come down in many drops to destroy sickness and death.

l: clouds, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXI.
s: The clouds are called to travel through the sky and air and descend upon the earth by thousands and myriads of drops. Their waters are asked to bring new waters, earth, trees, health, and healing powers.

l: sickness, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXI.
s: Sickness is to be destroyed altogether by the descending waters, including the sickness made by the Gaini. It is also driven away with other diseases created by Angra Mainyu's witchcraft.

l: death, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXI.
s: Death is to be destroyed altogether, including the death made by the Gaini. The text prays that healing will follow death and drives away all manner of deaths.

l: Gainis, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXI.
s: The Gaini makes sickness and death, and wicked Gainis are driven away. The Gahi is described as addicted to the Yâtu.

l: the sea Vouru-kasha, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXI.
s: The sea Vouru-kasha is the gathering place of waters. From it, waters are called to rise, travel through the aerial way, descend on the earth, and roll along.

l: Ahura Mazda, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXI.
s: Ahura Mazda made the aerial way, the earth, and everything grow through the rising and growing of waters and light. He grants a boon for holiness.

l: sun, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXI.
s: The swift-horsed sun is called to rise above Hara Berezaiti and produce light for the world along the path made by Mazda and the watery way opened by the gods.

l: Hara Berezaiti, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXI.
s: Hara Berezaiti is the place above which the sun, moon, and stars are called to rise and produce light for the world.

l: holy spell, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXI.
s: The holy spell keeps away evil by cleansing the birth and growth of a child and making a woman's body and strength pure. It makes the woman rich in children, milk, seed, fat, marrow, and offspring, and causes a thousand springs to flow toward pastures that feed the child.

l: woman, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXI.
s: The woman is made pure in body and strength and is made rich in children and milk. She is also described as rich in seed, fat, marrow, and offspring.

l: moon, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXI.
s: The moon is called to rise above Hara Berezaiti and produce light for the world. It keeps in itself the seed of the bull.

l: stars, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXI.
s: The stars are said to have in them the seed of waters. They are called to rise above Hara Berezaiti and produce light for the world.

l: Angra Mainyu, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXI.
s: Angra Mainyu has created disease, rottenness, and infection against the bodies of mortals by his witchcraft. These afflictions are driven away.

l: Airyaman, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXI.
s: Airyaman is called to come for the men and women of Zarathustra and the faithful to rejoice. He is asked to smite all manner of diseases and deaths, Yâtus, Pairikas, and wicked Gainis.

l: faithful, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXI.
s: The faithful are promised gifts from the holy bull and are included among those for whom Airyaman is asked to come and bring rejoicing. A desirable reward and a boon for holiness are associated with them.

l: Drug, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXI.
s: The fiendish Drug is commanded to perish, along with the brood and world of the fiend. It is driven away toward the regions of the north so that it will no longer give the living world of the holy spirit to death.

l: Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXII.
s: Ahura Mazda tells Spitama Zarathustra that Angra Mainyu created many diseases through witchcraft after looking at the mansion made by Ahura Mazda. Ahura Mazda asks Mãthra Spenta and then Airyaman to heal him, offering sacrifices and a holy blessing-spell in return. Ahura Mazda sends Nairyô-sangha to deliver the request to Airyaman. Airyaman comes with animals and nine twigs, draws nine furrows, and drives away diseases, deaths, demons, and other afflictions.

l: Ahura Mazda, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXII.
s: Ahura Mazda made the beautiful, shining mansion seen afar. He says that Angra Mainyu afflicted him with many diseases, asks Mãthra Spenta and Airyaman to heal him, offers sacrifices and a holy blessing-spell in return, and sends Nairyô-sangha to summon Airyaman.

l: Zarathustra, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXII.
s: Spitama Zarathustra is addressed by Ahura Mazda in this unit.

l: the mansion (made by Ahura Mazda), Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXII.
s: The mansion is described as beautiful, shining, and seen afar. Ahura Mazda says that he made it and that he may go up there and pass there.

l: Angra Mainyu, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXII.
s: Angra Mainyu is called the ruffian and the deadly one. He looked at Ahura Mazda and wrought many diseases by his witchcraft against the bodies of mortals.

l: diseases (created by Angra Mainyu), Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXII.
s: The diseases include nine, ninety, nine hundred, nine thousand, and nine times ten thousand diseases. Airyaman drives away diseases, deaths, pain, fever, rottenness, and infection created by Angra Mainyu.

l: Mãthra Spenta, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXII.
s: Mãthra Spenta is called the most glorious and all-glorious. Ahura Mazda asks Mãthra Spenta to heal him, and Mãthra Spenta asks how the diseases can be driven away.

l: Airyaman, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXII.
s: Airyaman is called the much-desired. After receiving Ahura Mazda's message through Nairyô-sangha, Airyaman comes with nine stallions, nine camels, nine bulls, nine head of small cattle, nine twigs, and nine furrows, and drives away diseases, deaths, Yâtus, Pairikas, and wicked Gainis.

l: Nairyô-sangha, Vendidad (Vendîdâd), Fargard XXII.
s: Nairyô-sangha is the herald whom Ahura Mazda calls and sends toward the mansion of Airyaman. He delivers Ahura Mazda's message and request for healing to Airyaman.

l: Sirozahs (Sîrôzahs), Sirozahs (Sîrôzahs), Sirozahs (Sîrôzahs) / Sîrôzah I. .. Sîrôzah II.
s: This unit presents Sîrôzah I and II, prayers and sacrifices addressed to Ahura Mazda, the Amesha-Spentas, and many other divine beings. Ahura Mazda is invoked as bright and glorious and as the Maker. The Amesha-Spentas are repeatedly invoked or sacrificed to as beneficent and all-ruling, and each is associated with particular virtues or sacred powers. The text also names waters, plants, stars, winds, Fravashis, mountains, laws, and other beings honored in the prayers.

l: Ahura Mazda, Sirozahs (Sîrôzahs), Sirozahs (Sîrôzahs) / Sîrôzah I. .. Sîrôzah II.
s: Ahura Mazda is invoked as bright and glorious and is called the Maker. The prayers and sacrifices are offered to him, and many beings, places, objects, and powers are described as made by Mazda.

l: Amesha-Spentas, Sirozahs (Sîrôzahs), Sirozahs (Sîrôzahs) / Sîrôzah I. .. Sîrôzah II.
s: The Amesha-Spentas are invoked alongside Ahura Mazda in Sîrôzah I and are sacrificed to as all-ruling and all-beneficent in Sîrôzah II. Individual Amesha-Spentas, including Vohu-Manô, Asha-Vahista, Khshathra-Vairya, Spenta-Ârmaiti, Haurvatât, and Ameretât, are associated with specific virtues, powers, or forms of prosperity.

l: Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, I. Ormazd Yast.
s: This unit concerns Ahura Mazda, Zarathustra, the Amesha-Spentas, and the Holy Word. Zarathustra asks which part of the Holy Word is strongest and most effective, and Ahura Mazda answers that his names are strongest, victorious, glorious, healing, and fiend-smiting. Ahura Mazda reveals twenty names and teaches that reciting them protects a person from weapons, fiends, and harm. The unit also praises holiness, good thoughts, words, and deeds, and invokes protection, health, prosperity, strength, and long life.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, I. Ormazd Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda is praised as bright and glorious, the Maker of the material world, the Holy One, and the most beneficent Spirit. He answers Zarathustra's questions, reveals his names, promises help and joy, and is invoked to destroy Angra Mainyu, Daêvas, fiends, and malice.

l: Angra Mainyu, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, I. Ormazd Yast.
s: Angra Mainyu is identified as the fiend who is all death and as the enemy whom Ahura Mazda is invoked to destroy. Reciting Ahura Mazda's names protects a person from him.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, I. Ormazd Yast.
s: Zarathustra asks Ahura Mazda which part of the Holy Word is strongest, most victorious, glorious, effective, healing, and fiend-smiting. He is instructed to recite Ahura Mazda's names and later says that he threw a ruffian back into the earth and made him powerless through Spenta-Ârmaiti.

l: Amesha-Spentas, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, I. Ormazd Yast.
s: The Amesha-Spentas are worshipped with sacrifice, prayer, propitiation, and glorification, and their names are identified as the strongest part of the Holy Word. They are described as Ahura Mazda's creatures, and their help and joy are invoked.

l: Holy Word, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, I. Ormazd Yast.
s: The Holy Word is described as having a strongest, most victorious, most glorious, most effective, most fiend-smiting, and best-healing part. Ahura Mazda says that his names constitute this part.

l: Good Thoughts, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, I. Ormazd Yast.
s: Good thoughts, good words, and good deeds are praised, embraced, and associated with the foremost wish of God. Evil thoughts, evil words, and evil deeds are rejected.

l: Ashem Vohû, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, I. Ormazd Yast.
s: Holiness is declared to be the best of all good and is identified with the law of holiness. It is repeatedly praised, worshipped, and presented as the principle perfected by the holy ones.

l: Daêvas, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, I. Ormazd Yast.
s: Daêvas are hated and opposed under the laws of Ahura. Ahura Mazda's names are said to destroy their malice, and the names are invoked to afflict and smite them.

l: Vohu-Manô, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, I. Ormazd Yast.
s: Vohu-Manô is one of Ahura Mazda's creatures and is associated with the riches given to those who work for Mazda and relieve the poor. Vohu-Manô is also said to come with Sraosha to help whomsoever Ahura Mazda pleases.

l: Asha-Vahista, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, I. Ormazd Yast.
s: Asha-Vahista is one of Ahura Mazda's creatures and is worshipped as most fair, undying, and beneficent. The unit also invokes the holy creations of Asha-Vahista.

l: Khsathra-Vairya, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, I. Ormazd Yast.
s: Khsathra-Vairya is named among the creatures of Ahura Mazda.

l: Spenta-Ârmaiti, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, I. Ormazd Yast.
s: Spenta-Ârmaiti is named among the creatures of Ahura Mazda and is associated with the holy creation. Through the eyes or help of Spenta-Ârmaiti, a ruffian's power is broken and the malice of enemies is to be shattered.

l: Sraosha, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, I. Ormazd Yast.
s: Sraosha is described as good and holy and is invoked to come for help and joy. Sraosha is also said to come with Vohu-Manô to help whomsoever Ahura Mazda pleases.

l: material world, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, I. Ormazd Yast.
s: The material world is said to come to the fulfilment of its wishes and to be freed from the anxieties of the heart through the strongest part of the Holy Word. Ahura Mazda is identified as its Maker.

l: sacrifice and prayer, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, I. Ormazd Yast.
s: Sacrifice and prayer are offered to the Amesha-Spentas, Ahura Mazda, and other holy beings with propitiation and glorification. They are also used in offerings of libations and are associated with blessings, protection, health, prosperity, and strength.

l: the names of Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, I. Ormazd Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda reveals twenty names, including the One of whom questions are asked, the Herd-giver, Perfect Holiness, Understanding, Knowledge, Weal, AHURA, the Creator, and MAZDA. Reciting and pronouncing these names by day or night is said to protect a person from weapons, fiends, malice, and harm.

l: Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, II. Haptân Yast.
s: The unit concerns worship, sacrifice, prayer, and glorification offered to Ahura Mazda, the Amesha-Spentas, and other holy beings. It names their attributes and associations across the five Gâhs, including Vohu-Manô, Asha-Vahista, Spenta-Ârmaiti, and Sraosha. Zarathustra is told that Yâtus, Daêvas, men, and Drug are crushed or destroyed through the protective power of the Amesha-Spentas and the observance of Mazda's laws. The unit concludes by blessing these acts and asking for brightness, glory, health, strength, welfare, offspring, long life, and the blissful abode of the holy Ones.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, II. Haptân Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda is described as bright and glorious and receives sacrifice, prayer, propitiation, and glorification. He is associated with the Amesha-Spentas and with the making of wisdom, Saoka, Gaokerena, and the waters.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, II. Haptân Yast.
s: Zarathustra is addressed as the one to whom it is declared that the Yâtus should be crushed. He is told about the person who destroys Drug, takes the seven Amesha-Spentas as a shield, renounces trespasses and faults, and restores the Law of Mazda.

l: Amesha-Spentas, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, II. Haptân Yast.
s: The Amesha-Spentas are described as all-ruling and all-beneficent, and sacrifice is offered to them. Their sevenfold presence is taken as a shield against enemies.

l: Vohu-Manô, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, II. Haptân Yast.
s: Vohu-Manô is named as an Amesha-Spenta and receives sacrifice, prayer, propitiation, and glorification. The destroyer of Vohu-Manô and his words is thrown down with repeated preaching and smiting.

l: Asha-Vahista, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, II. Haptân Yast.
s: Asha-Vahista is called the fairest and is named among the Amesha-Spentas. Sacrifice is offered to Asha-Vahista, who is also invoked at the Gâh Rapithwin.

l: Spenta-Ârmaiti, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, II. Haptân Yast.
s: Spenta-Ârmaiti is called good and receives sacrifice, prayer, propitiation, and glorification. She is associated with the good Râta, made by Mazda and holy.

l: Sraosha, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, II. Haptân Yast.
s: Sraosha is described as holy, devout, tall-formed, and fiend-smiting, and as making the world grow. Sacrifice, prayer, propitiation, and glorification are offered to Sraosha at the Gâh Usahin.

l: Daêvas, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, II. Haptân Yast.
s: The speaker declares hatred of the Daêvas and obedience to the laws of Ahura. Daêvas are included among those whom the Yâtus should crush.

l: the Law of the worshippers of Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, II. Haptân Yast.
s: The Law of the worshippers of Mazda is worshipped. It is named alongside the waters coming in the shape of a horse, made by Mazda.

l: Law of Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, II. Haptân Yast.
s: The Law of Mazda is described as having been carried away as a prisoner into the hands of the ungodly. A person who destroys the destroyer of Vohu-Manô takes the Law of Mazda away from them.

l: sacrifice, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, II. Haptân Yast.
s: Sacrifice is offered to Ahura Mazda, the Amesha-Spentas, and many other holy beings. The sacrifice is blessed together with prayer, strength, and vigour, and is associated with requests for prosperity and well-being.

l: prayer, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, II. Haptân Yast.
s: Prayer is offered with sacrifice, propitiation, and glorification to Ahura Mazda and the holy beings. The prayer is blessed together with strength and vigour.

l: Law of holiness, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, II. Haptân Yast.
s: The Law of holiness is stated in the formula, “The will of the Lord is the law of holiness.” The formula appears after worship and again after the account of crushing evil.

l: Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, III. Ardibehist Yast.
s: Ardibehist Yast concerns Ahura Mazda, Spitama Zarathustra, Asha-Vahista, and the Amesha-Spentas. Ahura Mazda instructs Zarathustra to increase Asha-Vahista through hymns, worship, sacrifice, blessings, and adoration, and Zarathustra asks for the proper words. The Airyaman prayer is praised as the greatest and most healing of spells, driving away sickness, Death, Daêvas, and other harmful forces. Angra Mainyu fears Asha-Vahista, while the Drug is driven toward the northern regions and the holy are promised brightness, glory, health, and a blissful abode.

l: Ardibehist Yast, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, III. Ardibehist Yast.
s: It presents teachings and praises concerning Asha-Vahista, the Airyaman prayer, healing, and the defeat of harmful forces.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, III. Ardibehist Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda speaks unto Spitama Zarathustra and instructs him to increase Asha-Vahista through hymns, worship, invocations, sacrifice, blessings, and adoration. He is associated with Good Thoughts, Good Words, and Good Deeds, and keeps the Garô-nmâna.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, III. Ardibehist Yast.
s: Spitama Zarathustra asks Ahura Mazda for the right words so that he may increase Asha-Vahista through worship and sacred acts.

l: Asha-Vahista, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, III. Ardibehist Yast.
s: Asha-Vahista is the fairest Amesha-Spenta and a god who smites sickness, Death, Daêvas, counter-work, Ashemaogha, and oppressors of men. His brightness, glory, strength, and vigour are praised and offered sacrifice.

l: Amesha-Spentas, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, III. Ardibehist Yast.
s: The Amesha-Spentas are invoked through sacrifice and prayer. The way to their abode is made easy by proclaiming Asha-Vahista.

l: Angra Mainyu, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, III. Ardibehist Yast.
s: Angra Mainyu, who is all death and the worst-lying of all Daêvas, rushes away from Asha-Vahista and cries out in fear of his power.

l: Daêvas, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, III. Ardibehist Yast.
s: The Daêvas and their counter-work flee before the Airyaman prayer and are smitten by Asha-Vahista. They are described as among the forces defeated by the prayer.

l: Garô-nmâna, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, III. Ardibehist Yast.
s: The Garô-nmâna is the abode of Ahura Mazda for holy souls. No wicked person can enter it or its bright, wide, holy ways.

l: Ashemaogha, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, III. Ardibehist Yast.
s: The unholy Ashemaogha flees before the Airyaman prayer and is smitten and afflicted by Asha-Vahista.

l: Law of holiness, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, III. Ardibehist Yast.
s: Holiness is called the best of all good. It is presented as a means of healing and as the law associated with the will of the Lord.

l: Holy Word, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, III. Ardibehist Yast.
s: The Holy Word is one of the means by which healing may be performed. Healing with the Holy Word is described as the best-healing of all remedies.

l: Airyaman prayer, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, III. Ardibehist Yast.
s: The Airyaman prayer smites the strength of the creatures of Angra Mainyu, the Yâtus, and Pairikas. It is called the greatest, fairest, firmest, most victorious, and best-healing of spells, and it drives away sickness, Death, Daêvas, and other harmful forces.

l: sickness, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, III. Ardibehist Yast.
s: Sickness flees before the Airyaman prayer and is smitten by Asha-Vahista. The prayer is said to drive sickness away from the body of the faithful.

l: Death, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, III. Ardibehist Yast.
s: Death flees before the Airyaman prayer and is smitten by Asha-Vahista. Angra Mainyu is described as all death.

l: sacrifice, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, III. Ardibehist Yast.
s: Sacrifice is used to praise and increase Asha-Vahista and to invoke the Amesha-Spentas. Libations, Haoma and meat, baresma, holy spells, speech, deeds, and rightly-spoken words are offered in sacrifice.

l: prayer, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, III. Ardibehist Yast.
s: Prayer is used with hymns, invocations, holy words, sacrifice, blessings, and adoration to increase Asha-Vahista. Sacrifice and prayer are blessed along with the strength and vigour of Asha-Vahista, Airyaman, and Saoka.

l: spells, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, III. Ardibehist Yast.
s: The Airyaman prayer is described as the greatest, fairest, most fearful, firmest, most victorious, and best-healing of spells. Its power drives away sickness, Death, Daêvas, and other harmful forces.

l: Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IV. Khordâd Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda tells Spitama Zarathustra that Haurvatât provides help, enjoyments, comforts, and pleasures for the faithful. Invoking Haurvatât and the other Amesha-Spentas smites the Nasu and other harmful beings and frees the faithful man from their attacks. The faithful man separates from the wicked by pronouncing Ahura Mazda’s spell, drawing three, six, or nine furrows, and binding and striking down the Drug. The unit prescribes that the spell be transmitted only within specified relationships and concludes with sacrifice, prayer, and blessings for Haurvatât, the prosperity of the seasons, and the years.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IV. Khordâd Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda speaks unto Spitama Zarathustra about the benefits of Haurvatât and the Amesha-Spentas. He explains how the faithful man parts from the wicked and prescribes the proper transmission of the spell.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IV. Khordâd Yast.
s: Spitama Zarathustra receives Ahura Mazda’s teachings about Haurvatât, the faithful man, the Drug, and the spell. He is instructed not to show the spell except in the specified circumstances.

l: Haurvatât, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IV. Khordâd Yast.
s: Haurvatât is an Amesha-Spenta and master who provides help, enjoyments, comforts, and pleasures for the faithful. Sacrifice, prayer, propitiation, glorification, libations, Haoma, meat, baresma, wisdom of the tongue, holy spells, speech, deeds, and rightly-spoken words are offered unto Haurvatât.

l: Amesha-Spentas, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IV. Khordâd Yast.
s: The Amesha-Spentas include Vohu-Manô, Asha-Vahista, Khshathra-Vairya, Spenta-Ârmaiti, Haurvatât, and Ameretât. Their names smite men turned to Nasus by the Druges, and heavenly Yazatas in company with them free the faithful man from harmful beings.

l: Daêvas, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IV. Khordâd Yast.
s: The Daêvas are hated by the worshipper of Mazda and opposed by the faithful. Haurvatât’s name is invoked against their thousands, ten thousands, and numberless myriads.

l: faithful man, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IV. Khordâd Yast.
s: The faithful man is proclaimed first of men and is freed by Rashnu Razista and the heavenly Yazatas from the Nasu, harmful beings, wicked men, and other threats. He separates from the wicked by pronouncing Ahura Mazda’s spell and drawing three, six, or nine furrows.

l: Nasu, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IV. Khordâd Yast.
s: The Nasu is smitten by invoking Haurvatât and by the names of the Amesha-Spentas. It is struck with bruising and deadly blows after the sun goes down for the propitiation and glorification of the heavenly gods.

l: Drug, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IV. Khordâd Yast.
s: The Drug is addressed and smitten, bound, thrown down, and driven away from the Aryan countries by the spell. The Druges defile by open ways, hidden ways, or contact, and turn men toward Nasus.

l: Law of holiness, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IV. Khordâd Yast.
s: The law of holiness is identified with the will of the Lord in the Yathâ ahû vairyô prayer. The faithful follow it, and those devoted to the good law can still the Druges.

l: the law of holiness, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IV. Khordâd Yast.
s: Holiness is declared to be the best of all good. Haurvatât, the prosperity of the seasons, and the years are described as masters of holiness.

l: holy spells, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IV. Khordâd Yast.
s: The spell is used to smite, bind, and throw down the Drug and to separate the way of the faithful from the way of the wicked. It may be shown only by a father to his son, a brother to his brother from the same womb, or an Âthravan to a qualified pupil.

l: sacrifice and prayer, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IV. Khordâd Yast.
s: Sacrifice is offered unto Hâvani, Haurvatât, the prosperity of the seasons, and the years. It includes libations, Haoma and meat, baresma, wisdom of the tongue, holy spells, speech, deeds, and rightly-spoken words.

l: prayer, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IV. Khordâd Yast.
s: Prayer is joined with sacrifice, propitiation, and glorification for Hâvani, Haurvatât, the prosperity of the seasons, and the years. The Yathâ ahû vairyô and Ashem Vohû prayers are recited or invoked.

l: Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, V. Âbân Yast.
s: This unit concerns Ardvi Sûra Anâhita, the holy, health-giving spring and river created and praised under Ahura Mazda. Ahura Mazda tells Spitama Zarathustra to offer sacrifices to her, describing her waters, channels, powers, and benefits for people, animals, lands, and fertility. Many figures request boons from Ardvi Sûra Anâhita through sacrifice and libations; she grants some requests and refuses others. The unit also recounts her aid to Vafra Navâza and Vistauru and describes conflicts involving Azi Dahâka, Thraêtaona, and the Aryan people.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, V. Âbân Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda tells Spitama Zarathustra to offer sacrifice to Ardvi Sûra Anâhita. He is said to have brought her waters down with mighty vigour and to have offered her a sacrifice in Airyana Vaêgah, where he received the boon of bringing Zarathustra to follow his law.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, V. Âbân Yast.
s: Spitama Zarathustra is instructed to offer sacrifice to Ardvi Sûra Anâhita. He is identified as the son of Pourushaspa and as the person whom Ahura Mazda sought to bring to think, speak, and act according to his law.

l: Ardvi Sûra Anâhita, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, V. Âbân Yast.
s: Ardvi Sûra Anâhita is a wide-expanding, health-giving, holy spring and river who hates the Daêvas and obeys the laws of Ahura. Her waters increase life, herds, folds, wealth, and countries; purify male seed and female wombs; and provide milk to females. She grants many requested boons, refuses some, and appears in the shape of a strong, radiant maid to rescue Vafra Navâza and aid Vistauru.

l: Daêvas, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, V. Âbân Yast.
s: The Daêvas are opposed by Ardvi Sûra Anâhita and by those who worship Ahura Mazda. They are described as enemies, with two thirds of the Daêvas of Mâzana being smitten by Haoshyangha, and they are involved in the conflicts and requests made by several figures.

l: waters that run along the earth, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, V. Âbân Yast.
s: The good Waters are made by Mazda and receive propitiation with sacrifice, prayer, and glorification. They are associated with Ardvi Sûra Anâhita and with all waters made by Mazda.

l: water, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, V. Âbân Yast.
s: Water flows from Ardvi Sûra Anâhita across the seven Karshvares, both in summer and winter. Her waters purify seed and wombs, provide milk, and can be made partly still or partly flowing to create a dry passage.

l: libations, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, V. Âbân Yast.
s: Libations are to be cleanly prepared and well strained and offered with Haoma and meat. Figures who request boons give libations, gifts, and sacrifice, and Ardvi Sûra Anâhita grants or refuses their requests in that context.

l: sacrifice, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, V. Âbân Yast.
s: Sacrifice is repeatedly commanded for Ardvi Sûra Anâhita and is offered with prayer, propitiation, glorification, libations, Haoma, meat, baresma, holy spells, words, and deeds. Ahura Mazda and numerous human figures perform sacrifices to seek her favor and boons.

l: boon, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, V. Âbân Yast.
s: A boon is requested from Ardvi Sûra Anâhita by Ahura Mazda and by many other figures. She grants boons involving sovereignty, victory, rescue, safe passage, and aid, but refuses requests from Azi Dahâka, Frangrasyan, and the sons of Vaêsaka.

l: sea Vouru-Kasha, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, V. Âbân Yast.
s: Vouru-Kasha is the sea into which Ardvi Sûra Anâhita runs from Hukairya. Its shores and middle are described as boiling over, and it is the place where Frangrasyan seeks to seize the Glory belonging to the Aryan people and where Keresâspa seeks to overcome Gandarewa.

l: Hukairya, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, V. Âbân Yast.
s: Hukairya is the height from which Ardvi Sûra Anâhita runs down toward Vouru-Kasha. Yima Khshaêta offers sacrifice to her from this height.

l: Karshvares, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, V. Âbân Yast.
s: The seven Karshvares are the regions over which the waters of Ardvi Sûra Anâhita spread. Azi Dahâka asks for a boon that would make all seven empty of men, but Ardvi Sûra Anâhita refuses it.

l: Drug, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, V. Âbân Yast.
s: Azi Dahâka, the three-mouthed, offers sacrifice to Ardvi Sûra Anâhita in the land of Bawri and asks that all the seven Karshvares be emptied of men. She does not grant his boon. He is also described as a three-headed, six-eyed, powerful fiendish Drug whom Thraêtaona overcomes.

l: Thraêtaona, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, V. Âbân Yast.
s: Thraêtaona, heir of the valiant Âthwya clan, offers sacrifice to Ardvi Sûra Anâhita and asks for the power to overcome Azi Dahâka and rescue his two wives. Ardvi Sûra Anâhita grants him that boon.

l: the Aryan people, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, V. Âbân Yast.
s: The Aryan people are associated with the Glory in the middle of Vouru-Kasha, which Frangrasyan seeks but is not granted. They are also mentioned as including those born and those not yet born, and as people whose enemies are defeated in requests made to Ardvi Sûra Anâhita.

l: Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XX.
s: This unit concerns Ardvi Sûra Anâhita, the spring whom Spitama Zarathustra and others worship through sacrifices, libations, gifts, prayers, and entreaties. Ahura Mazda orders Ardvi Sûra Anâhita to descend from the stars to protect creation, and she is described as a powerful water whose channels, palaces, appearance, clothing, and attendants are detailed. She grants requested boons to Yôista, Zarathustra, Kavi Vîstâspa, and Zairi-vairi, but refuses the request of Aregat-aspa and Vandaremaini to conquer Vîstâspa and Zairi-vairi. The text also explains which people may drink her libations and that Daêvas receive libations offered after sunset.

l: Ardvi Sûra Anâhita, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XX.
s: Ardvi Sûra Anâhita is a powerful holy spring and water who protects the creation made by Ahura Mazda. She grants or refuses boons in response to sacrifices, libations, gifts, and entreaties, and is described as descending from the stars, wearing golden ornaments and beaver garments, and possessing a thousand cells and channels.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XX.
s: Spitama Zarathustra is repeatedly instructed to offer sacrifices to Ardvi Sûra Anâhita. He asks her how to worship and forward her, offers her a sacrifice in Airyana Vaêgah, and receives the boon that he may bring Kavi Vîstâspa to think, speak, and act according to the law.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XX.
s: Ahura Mazda orders Ardvi Sûra Anâhita to descend from the stars to the earth so that great lords, masters of countries, their sons, and others may worship her. He establishes Spitama Zarathustra as master of the material world and Ardvi Sûra Anâhita as keeper of the holy creation.

l: libations, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XX.
s: Libations are offered to Ardvi Sûra Anâhita together with sacrifices, gifts, prayers, and entreaties. She says that qualified Âthravan priests may drink them, while various disqualified people may not; libations offered after sunset are received by six hundred and a thousand Daêvas.

l: sacrifice, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XX.
s: Sacrifices to Ardvi Sûra Anâhita are made with libations, gifts, prayers, spells, Haoma, meat, baresma, speech, deeds, and rightly spoken words. Through such sacrifices, worshippers request victory, prosperity, knowledge, good husbands, safe delivery, swift horses, and other favours.

l: Daêvas, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XX.
s: Daêvas receive libations brought to Ardvi Sûra Anâhita after the sun has set. Six hundred and a thousand of them receive those libations while howling, clapping, hopping, and shouting.

l: Hukairya, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XX.
s: Hukairya is a golden height of deep precipices from which Ardvi Sûra Anâhita leaps. She is said to descend from it with great force and with as much Glory as all the waters running along the earth.

l: Kavi Vîstâspa, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XX.
s: Vîstâspa is the son of Aurvat-aspa and a Kavi who is associated with the Naotaras and the swiftest horses in the countries. Ardvi Sûra Anâhita grants him victory-related boons and is asked to help Zarathustra bring him to think, speak, and act according to the law.

l: Aregat-aspa, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XX.
s: Aregat-aspa is described as wicked and as a worshipper or follower of the bad law. Ardvi Sûra Anâhita grants a boon against him to Kavi Vîstâspa and Zairi-vairi, but refuses his own request, made with Vandaremaini, to conquer Vîstâspa and Zairi-vairi.

l: Zairi-vairi, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XX.
s: Zairi-vairi is a mounted fighter who offers a sacrifice to Ardvi Sûra Anâhita and receives the boon of overcoming Peshô-Kangha, Humâyaka, and the wicked Aregat-aspa. He is later named as one of the Aryan opponents whom Aregat-aspa and Vandaremaini fail to conquer.

l: Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VI. Khôrshêd Yast.
s: This unit is a Yast to the undying, shining, swift-horsed Sun and concerns its worship, power, and protection against darkness and harmful beings. When the sun rises, the earth made by Ahura, waters, and holy creatures become clean, while heavenly Yazatas gather and pour its Glory upon the earth. The Daêvas would destroy the things in the seven Karshvares if the sun did not rise. Sacrifice to the Sun is offered to Ahura Mazda, the Amesha-Spentas, and the worshipper's own soul, and Mithra is praised in connection with the Sun.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VI. Khôrshêd Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda is the being to whom sacrifice to the undying, shining, swift-horsed Sun is offered. The earth made by Ahura is described as becoming clean when the sun rises.

l: Daêvas, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VI. Khôrshêd Yast.
s: The Daêvas are hated and opposed through the laws of Ahura and through sacrifice to the Sun. They are born of darkness, and if the sun did not rise they would destroy all things in the seven Karshvares.

l: undying, shining, swift-horsed Sun, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VI. Khôrshêd Yast.
s: The undying, shining, swift-horsed Sun is the subject of the Yast and receives sacrifice, prayer, propitiation, glorification, libations, Haoma and meat, baresma, holy spells, speech, and deeds. When it rises, it makes the earth, waters, and holy creatures clean, and its light withstands darkness, the Daêvas, robbers and bandits, Yâtus and Pairikas, and unseen death.

l: the law of holiness, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VI. Khôrshêd Yast.
s: Holiness is declared to be the best of all good and the law of the Lord. The unit seeks the increase of the world and creatures of holiness.

l: heavenly Yazatas, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VI. Khôrshêd Yast.
s: The heavenly Yazatas stand up by hundreds and thousands when the sun's light and brightness wax warmer. They gather the Sun's Glory, make it pass down, and pour it upon the earth made by Ahura, and they are rejoiced by sacrifice to the Sun.

l: the earth made by Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VI. Khôrshêd Yast.
s: The earth made by Ahura becomes clean when the sun rises. The heavenly Yazatas pour the Sun's Glory upon it for the increase of the world of holiness.

l: Mithra, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VI. Khôrshêd Yast.
s: Mithra is called the lord of wide pastures and is described as having a thousand ears and ten thousand eyes. His club is offered sacrifice, and the friendship between the moon and the sun is called the best of all friendships.

l: sacrifice, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VI. Khôrshêd Yast.
s: Sacrifice is offered to the undying, shining, swift-horsed Sun to withstand darkness, the Daêvas, robbers and bandits, Yâtus and Pairikas, and unseen death. Such sacrifice is offered to Ahura Mazda, the Amesha-Spentas, and the worshipper's own soul, and it rejoices the heavenly and worldly Yazatas.
